Problem stem: Let $g(x) = \dfrac{x^2 - 9}{x + 3}$. Is $g$ continuous at $x = -3$? Justify using the three-part definition.

Problem stem: Consider $h(x) = \begin{cases} 3x - 2 & x < 1 \\ 4 & x = 1 \\ x^2 & x > 1 \end{cases}$. Determine whether $h$ is continuous at $x = 1$ and classify any discontinuity.
Available first step: Evaluate the left-hand limit $\lim_{x \to 1^-} h(x)$ using the piece $3x - 2$.

Available first step: Recall all three conditions in the definition of continuity and identify which one the classmate hasn't verified.
